svg.text: Pi 4 Model B → ESP32 DevKit V1 (30-pin): pin-to-pin wiring
11 wires: 6 for the safety test, 2 shared UART0 (flash + telemetry), 2 flash control (EN, BOOT), 1 power. Resistors 330 Ω–1 kΩ in series on every signal wire.
GPIO14 TXD → RX0 flash data + commands
GPIO15 RXD ← TX0 flash reply + telemetry
GPIO24 → BOOT button leg (GPIO0) bootloader select
Indicator LEDs (optional, so the bug is visible)
D19 → 330 Ω → LED long leg, LED short leg → GND rail (actuator)
D21 → 330 Ω → LED long leg, LED short leg → GND rail (safety relay)
BOOT wire: GPIO0 isn't on this board's header, only on the BOOT button.
Solder a short wire to the BOOT button leg that is NOT ground (test with a multimeter:
the non-GND leg reads 3.3 V when idle), or skip the wire and hold BOOT by hand when
the console tells you to. EN is on the header (bottom-right pin on your board).
Power: Pi 5V pin 2 → VIN works with a 3 A Pi PSU. Or use a 5 V charger into micro-USB and skip pin 2.
Blue — Pi drives the ESP32 inputs (trigger, PWM, fault).
Orange — Pi reads the ESP32 outputs: the physical truth.
Purple — ESP32 TX0 → Pi RXD: telemetry (what the firmware claims) and flash replies.
Pink — flashing from the Pi: TXD → RX0 data, GPIO25 → EN reset, GPIO24 → BOOT (GPIO0).
Red — 5 V power to VIN. Never put 5 V on any GPIO.
Pi: raspi-config → Serial Port → login shell NO, hardware serial YES. RX0/TX0 are now owned by the Pi: no micro-USB data cable.
